title: 인사말 소리 내어 읽기: 감사합니다는 [감사함니다]
objective: You can read common greetings with their real sounds and choose the right greeting for a simple situation.
summary: Learners read everyday Korean greetings aloud with their real sounds.

task.title: Read and say greetings
task.line: Choose or write the real sound in [ ], then pick the right greeting for each situation.

words.meaning: hello (polite greeting to anyone, any time of day)
nice to meet you (said when meeting someone)
goodbye (said by the person leaving to the person staying)

letters.sound: A final ㅂ before ㄴ sounds [ㅁ]: 합니다 [함니다].
letters.as: Like 'm' in 'mom': close your lips and hum.

letters.sound: After final ㅂ, ㅅ sounds tense [ㅆ]: 반갑습니다 [반갑씀니다].
letters.as: ㅆ is a sharp 's' as in 'see', with little breath.

letters.sound: After a consonant (not ㄹ), ㅖ may sound [ㅔ]: 계세요 [게세요].
letters.as: ㅔ is like 'e' in 'get'; ㅖ is like 'ye' in 'yes'.

exercises: Choose the real sound: ① 고맙습니다 [고맙습니다 / 고맙씀니다] ② 미안합니다 [미안합니다 / 미안함니다]
Write the real sound in [ ]: ① 실례합니다 ② 사랑합니다 ③ 다행입니다
Can ㅖ be read as [ㅔ] here? Write Yes or No: ① 시계 ② 예, 알아요. ③ 차례

Write the right greeting from the word list: ① You are leaving a shop. The owner stays. ② You meet a new classmate for the first time and say you are glad to meet them. ③ You bump into someone on the subway and say sorry.
answers: ① Yes ([시게] is also correct) ② No (예 is always [예]) ③ No (례 keeps [례])
① 안녕히 계세요 ② 반갑습니다 (만나서 반갑습니다) ③ 죄송합니다
